root_cause.text: The __smc_setsockopt() function in net/smc performs a blocking user-space memory copy (copy_from_sockptr()) while holding the socket lock (lock_sock(sk)), allowing an attacker to stall execution indefinitely by supplying userfaultfd-monitored memory, causing a sleep-inside-lock condition that leads to a local denial of service.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description explicitly states this flaw: "The function __smc_setsockopt() calls copy_from_sockptr() while holding lock_sock(sk). By passing a userfaultfd-monitored memory page ... as the optval, an attacker can halt execution during the copy operation, keeping the lock held." The fix moves the copy_from_sockptr() call outside the lock_sock() critical section.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pre-fetch user data for SMC_LIMIT_HS setsockopt outside the socket lock to reduce lock hold time and avoid taking the lock on invalid input.
intent_record.what: Moved the optlen validation and copy_from_sockptr for SMC_LIMIT_HS setsockopt from inside the locked region (after lock_sock) to before acquiring the lock, and removed the corresponding break statements from the switch case.
intent_record.how: The validation and user-space data copy are now performed before taking the socket lock. Invalid arguments or copy failures cause early return without acquiring the lock. The assignment of smc->limit_smc_hs still happens under the lock after a successful copy.
